new_page.title: Minimum Down Payment in Canada: 5%, 10% or 20% (Examples)
new_page.h1: How much down payment do I need to buy a home?
new_page.description: 5% on the first $500,000, 10% on the rest up to $1.5 million, and 20% at $1.5 million or more. Worked examples at South Surrey and Langley prices.

breadcrumbs.name: How much down payment do I need to buy a home?

faq.q: Is mortgage insurance required with less than 20% down?
faq.a: Usually yes. The insurance premium is added to the mortgage, and the price limits for insured mortgages change from time to time, so ask your lender for the current rules.

faq.q: Does a down payment gift have to be paid back?
faq.a: No. Lenders accept gifts from immediate family with a letter saying the money does not have to be repaid.

parts.t: 5% of the first $500,000 of the price, plus 10% of the part from $500,000 to $1.5 million. At $1.5 million or more the minimum is 20%. With less than 20% down you will need mortgage default insurance.

blocks.text: Minimum down payment at common prices

parts.t: Property transfer tax (unless you are exempt), legal fees, a home inspection and adjustments for property tax and strata fees. Budget these separately from the down payment.

blocks.text: Where the down payment can come from

parts.t: Savings, an FHSA, the RRSP Home Buyers' Plan, and a gift from family with a signed gift letter. Your lender will ask for 90 days of history on most of it.
Read on November 18, 2026. Rules change, so confirm with the source or your lawyer, notary or accountant before you act.
